query: What additive manufacturing strategy and post-processing route can enable the fabrication of a refractory high-entropy alloy family (Group IV-V transition metals) capable of retaining high-temperature structural integrity, and what specific microstructural state is hypothesized to optimize mechanical performance while mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitial impurities?

generation.hypothesis: Fabrication of a Group IV-V refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) followed by a rapid thermal quench post-processing route will yield a metastable single-phase BCC microstructure with suppressed interstitial segregation, thereby optimizing high-temperature structural integrity and mitigating brittleness.
generation.material_initial_state: Powder blend of Group IV (Hf, Zr, Ti) and Group V (V, Nb, Ta) transition metals with trace interstitial impurities (C, N, O), exhibiting a tendency for compositional striations and brittle intermetallic formation upon slow cooling.
generation.intervention: Additive manufacturing via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using high volumetric energy density to induce rapid solidification, followed by immediate water quenching or cryogenic cooling to bypass equilibrium phase separation.
generation.conditions: Processing in an inert argon atmosphere with controlled oxygen content (<10 ppm); post-processing cooling rates >1000 K/s to suppress diffusion-controlled precipitation.
generation.structural_mediator: Metastable single-phase Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) solid solution stabilized by high configurational entropy and suppressed by rapid cooling kinetics, preventing the formation of brittle sigma or Laves phases and segregating interstitials into a supersaturated solid solution.
generation.mechanism: The high cooling rate inherent to SLM, combined with rapid post-processing quenching, kinetically traps the alloy in a high-entropy single-phase BCC state (similar to the computationally predicted stability in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf systems with VEC < 4.4), while the rapid thermal history prevents the diffusion of interstitial impurities to grain boundaries where they would cause embrittlement. The high configurational entropy of mixing stabilizes the solid solution against phase separation, while the rapid quench prevents the nucleation of brittle intermetallics typically formed during conventional casting or slow cooling.
generation.predicted_outcome: The resulting material will exhibit a homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure with high yield strength at temperatures up to 1000°C, significantly reduced brittleness compared to cast counterparts, and retained structural integrity due to the suppression of interstitial segregation and brittle phase formation.
generation.baseline: Conventionally cast or slowly cooled Group IV-V RHEAs which typically exhibit multiphase microstructures (BCC + sigma/Laves), significant compositional segregation, and brittle failure modes due to interstitial impurity clustering.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to alloys with a Valence Electron Concentration (VEC) < 4.4 and assumes the presence of sufficient configurational entropy to stabilize the BCC phase; it may not hold for alloys with high VEC or those containing elements that form stable intermetallics regardless of cooling rate.
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical cooling rate required to fully suppress interstitial segregation in the specific Group IV-V system is not quantified in the provided evidence, and the long-term stability of the metastable single-phase BCC structure under prolonged high-temperature service (creep) remains unverified in the supplied records.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate a W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA via SLM with varying cooling rates (SLM only vs. SLM + water quench vs. SLM + furnace cool) and subject samples to high-temperature compression tests (up to 1000°C) and interstitial analysis (APT/EPMA).
measurements: Phase constitution via XRD and TEM
Interstitial concentration profiles via Atom Probe Tomography (APT)
Yield strength and fracture strain at 25°C and 1000°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the SLM + water quench samples exhibit multiphase microstructures (e.g., sigma phase), significant interstitial segregation at grain boundaries, or brittle fracture behavior at high temperatures comparable to the furnace-cooled baseline.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: W 31 Ta 34 Cr 5.0 V 27 Hf 3.0 alloy. Intervention: Irradiation-induced homogenization vs. unirradiated state. Processing: Atom Probe Tomography (APT) on as-deposited and irradiated samples. Test conditions: As-deposited vs. irradiated (10 dpa, 1073 K). Structure change: As-deposited showed compositional striations (W-Ta and Cr-V-Hf layers); irradiated part showed homogenization and no precipitation. Property change: Not stated (microstructural observation). Mechanism: Irradiation-induced ballistic mixing and atomic displacement cause homogenization; ODTT (~1120 K) coincides with irradiation temperature. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The APT results from the as-deposited sample demonstrated compositional striations that were not detected by EDX."

Intervention effect. Base system: W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA system. Intervention: Design strategy using VEC model and CALPHAD. Processing: Thermophysical parameter calculations, CALPHAD, Cluster Expansion, Monte Carlo. Test conditions: Computational screening of compositions. Structure change: Predicted single-phase BCC structure over wide temperature range; minimized VEC to enhance stability. Property change: Predicted high thermal stability and radiation resistance. Mechanism: Configurational entropy of mixing stabilizes solid solution; VEC < 4.4 enhances mechanical performance. Evidence: calculated. Quote: "The strategy then consists in finding a combination of elements that can lower the VEC value."

Intervention effect. Base system: CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (equiatomic, fcc structure). Intervention: Applied hydrostatic pressure up to ~41 GPa. Processing: In situ high-pressure synchrotron XRD using a diamond anvil cell (DAC) with helium as pressure-transmitting medium. Test conditions: Room temperature, pressure range 0 to ~41 GPa. Structure change: Polymorphic transition from face-centred-cubic (fcc) to hexagonal-close-packing (hcp) structure; transition starts at ~22 GPa and completes at ~41 GPa. Property change: Phase composition changed from 100% fcc to ~100% hcp; hcp phase retained at ambient pressure after decompression (irreversible transition). Mechanism: Transition driven by high pressure overcoming kinetic barriers; hcp structure is thermodynamically favourable at lower temperatures and high pressures. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Once the pressure approaches 22.1 GPa, extra diffraction peaks beside the (111) peak of fcc appeared"

Intervention effect. Base system: Pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy powder. Intervention: Additive manufacturing via Selective Laser Melting (SLM) using specific laser parameters. Processing: Laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern. Test conditions: Room temperature and high temperatures (25 °C to 900 °C) compression tests. Structure change: Formed FCC single-phase random solid solution with epitaxial growth grains, dislocation networks, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates (27.3 nm). Property change: Yield strength of 778.4 MPa at room temperature, significantly higher than annealed (254.2 MPa) and other AM-processed (519 MPa) HEAs. Mechanism: Outstanding mechanical properties attributed to dislocation network, fine grain size, and nano-sized Mn2O3 precipitates. Evidence: measured. Quote: "SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution."
